objections.claim: At candidate artifact sha256:ccfaeb61b948a47c47f8f719cdd32b6455847a304923d194dec77706b563a4c8, E6 claims its finite exhaustive battery genuinely proves that an oracle evaluates its claimed invariant and that only evaluator implementation form is deferred, but §6b expressly admits a deterministic lookup-table oracle can pass that entire author-known domain without evaluating the invariant and leaves independently defined semantics open for the implementation slice. The interim same-input agreement check detects variance only, so this deterministic attack remains green. Moreover, `product-1-oq-e6-determinism-deferral` and its referee record are narrowed to determinism/evaluator form, not semantic discrimination. Thus governance correction d and the frozen requirement for discriminating oracles remain unresolved; this is an admitted soundness gap, not merely an unspecified implementation mechanism.

Section 5(e)(iv)'s exclusive publish interval is not executable from the credential set the approach specifies. GitHub's `PUT/DELETE /app/installations/{installation_id}/suspended` endpoints require a JWT authenticating as the owning GitHub App; repository-admin credentials, installation tokens, and fine-grained PATs cannot call them ([GitHub REST Apps contract](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/apps/apps)). The approach records installation permission scopes but never requires the Eye to own/manage both Apps, places their App private keys under Eye-local custody, authenticates suspension with App JWTs, or tests that custody. Therefore the promised automated suspension/unsuspension and resulting platform-exclusive interval are unsupported, leaving the acknowledged Contents-write release-deletion capability live unless App ownership, private-key custody, JWT authentication, and fail-closed regressions are added.
